card.stem: The sketch shows the front door of a dwelling house. The external wall is a 400 mm concrete block wall with a full-fill insulated cavity. The wall is plastered on both sides. The doorframe, which is fixed in the wall is 150 mm × 80 mm. The highly insulated wooden door is 90 mm in thickness with 15 mm vertical sheeting on both sides.
card.questionText: To a scale of 1:5, draw a vertical section through the external wall, concrete lintels, doorframe and door. On your drawing show the typical construction details from 400 mm below to a level 400 mm above the concrete lintels. Include four typical dimensions.

rows.contextNote: Credit the best SEVEN acceptable details at 5 marks each, capped at 35. Marked details: concrete block inner leaf with 15 mm internal plaster; 200 mm full-fill cavity insulation; concrete block outer leaf with 19 mm render; wall ties; concrete lintels; stepped DPC; airtight tape; cavity closer; thermally broken door frame (150 × 80 mm); insulated external door (90 mm).
Four appropriate typical dimensions on the section.

rows.verbatim: Draughting, accuracy and scale (excellent, good, fair)
rows.contextNote: Draughting, accuracy and scale of the section: excellent 8, good 6, fair 4.

card.stem: The sketch shows the uninsulated attic space of a dwelling house. The homeowners wish to add insulation to the roof at ceiling joist level and around water storage tank. The ceiling joists are 200 mm × 40 mm.
card.questionText: Using notes and freehand sketches, show one suitable method of insulating the roof at ceiling joist level. Specify the type and thickness of insulation.

rows.verbatim: Method of insulating attic note & sketch (7 + 7 marks)
rows.contextNote: Note 7 and sketch 7. Such as: insulation roll cut to the width between the ceiling joists and packed tightly above the plasterboard, with further layers laid crosswise on top.

card.questionText: Explain, with the aid of notes and freehand sketches, any five of the following: strip foundation; fascia board; airtight tape; wind turbine; septic tank; dovetail joint; wall tie; cordless jigsaw; underfloor heating.

rows.contextNote: Explain any five of the nine terms. Each term is marked separately: primary communication of relevant information 6 and other communication 4, in notes or sketches (the scheme reserves no fixed split between them). Strip foundation: a simple, common foundation for homes; concrete reinforced with steel for tensile strength; the wall placed centrally with loads spread at 45° to the ground; used where the soil has a good bearing capacity. Fascia board: gives a finished appearance and protects the house from the weather; part of the eaves with the soffit; carries the gutters; usually wood, PVC or aluminium. Airtight tape: a highly adhesive tape used with an airtight membrane at every junction of building elements and around door and window frames, preventing draughts and heat loss. Wind turbine: converts wind energy into mechanical energy that generates electricity; sustainable, reducing reliance on fossil fuels; commercial wind farms or smaller domestic turbines; horizontal- or vertical-axis. Septic tank: an underground chamber that collects, stores and treats domestic wastewater; anaerobic bacteria break down solids, which settle as sludge; treated water returns to the ground through the percolation area. Dovetail joint: a common joint in drawer and box construction and quality furniture; the slope of the tail (1:8 hardwood, 1:6 softwood) gives its tensile strength; cut by hand or with a router jig. Wall tie: ties the two leaves of a cavity wall into one stable unit, embedded in the mortar; stainless steel or basalt fibre (less thermal bridging); lengths to suit the cavity. Cordless jigsaw: cuts shapes and curves with a reciprocating blade; battery powered, portable and safer without a lead; the base rests on the work and is pushed along; used on a range of materials. Underfloor heating: polyethylene pipes beneath the floor carry water heated by a heat pump; the floor becomes a large heat source with no cold spots and a constant temperature, replacing radiators; efficient at low temperatures.
